coldStart.note: WIN-1 includes HTTP request overhead + JSON parse on the cold call. Pure cold start (Wasm instantiation only) is ~15ms.

throughput.note: WIN-4 and WIN-5 use the zero-marshal binary protocol — eliminates per-string WIT marshal tax. WIN-5 is pure in-process Wasm with binary I/O.

marshaling.note: WIN-2 (binary over TCP) eliminates JSON. WIN-5 (in-process Wasm + binary protocol) eliminates marshaling entirely.

variance.reason: Wasm has no GC pauses, no JIT deopt storms

composability.reason: Same Wasm code runs in-process (WIN-3) or over HTTP (WIN-1)

security.reason: Each Wasm component is sandboxed, memory-bounded, capability-gated

finalVerdict.summary: Memory: WIN. Cold start: WIN ✅. Throughput: WIN ✅. Marshaling: WIN ✅.

winArchitectures.WIN-1: Long-running Wasm HTTP server — real Rust + Python Wasm components, pre-instantiated at startup
winArchitectures.WIN-2: Binary protocol over TCP — flat binary wire format, no JSON
winArchitectures.WIN-3: In-process Wasm — direct component calls, no network (composability win)

reproductionSteps: 1. Install Rust nightly + cargo-component + componentize-py + jco + wasm-tools + wizer
2. Build inventory: cargo +nightly component build --release --target wasm32-wasip2
3. Build fraud: componentize-py --wit-path ../wit --world fraud-service componentize app -o fraud.wasm
4. Transpile bindings: jco transpile inventory.wasm -o benchmarks/wasm-bindings/inventory-new
